content_units: Date-Night Shortlist at a Glance
Best fit for your constraints:   Palm Springs  ,   Knives Out  ,   Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse  ,   Crazy Rich Asians  , and   The Princess Bride  .

These five balance   fun  ,   chemistry  ,   strong rewatch energy  , and   casual-viewer accessibility   while mostly staying near your preferred runtime and avoiding heavy downer endings. I treated “under 2 hours 15 minutes preferred” as a strong preference, not a hard cutoff.
Ranked Date-Night Picks
Rank   Film   Runtime   Tone   Pacing   Casual-Viewer Accessibility   Why It Ranks Here
1   Palm Springs   90 min   witty, romantic, playful   brisk   very high   Short, funny, emotionally satisfying, and easy to enjoy together
2   Knives Out   131 min   clever, lively, crowd-pleasing   fast   very high   Great shared-watch energy; fun mystery without getting bleak
3   Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse   117 min   energetic, heartfelt, stylish   very fast   high   Best animated pick; visually exciting and uplifting
4   Crazy Rich Asians   121 min   glossy, funny, romantic   smooth   very high   Easy date-night comfort watch with charm and low emotional risk
5   The Princess Bride   98 min   warm, whimsical, funny   relaxed   high   Sweet, quotable, and light, though its fairy-tale style is a specific taste
Why These 5 Work Best
1) Palm Springs
-   Best overall date-night pick  .
- Tone: flirty, funny, slightly existential without becoming gloomy.
- Pacing: very tight; at 90 minutes it never drags.
- Accessibility: extremely easy for casual viewers—high concept, low homework.
Tradeoff:
It has a time-loop premise, so if you want something more grounded or traditionally romantic, it may feel a little quirky. But that same quirk is what makes it memorable and conversation-friendly.
2) Knives Out
- A strong “watch together and react together” movie.
- Tone: playful mystery with humor and personality.
- Pacing: fast, with constant reveals and character turns.
- Accessibility: one of the easiest modern mysteries for broad audiences.
Tradeoff:
It is less overtly romantic than the others, so it’s more of a   fun shared experience   than a swoony date film. Runtime is also close to your upper preference at 131 minutes.
3) Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
- Your   best animated inclusion   by a wide margin.
- Tone: vibrant, funny, sincere, uplifting.
- Pacing: very energetic and visually dense.
- Accessibility: strong for casual viewers, even non-superhero fans.
Tradeoff:

The style is intense and kinetic, so if your ideal date night is soft, cozy, and low-stimulation, this can feel more “exciting” than “intimate.” Still, it ends on a high and is one of the most crowd-pleasing picks here.
4) Crazy Rich Asians
- A polished, easy, romantic crowd-pleaser.
- Tone: glamorous, funny, emotionally warm.
- Pacing: smooth and very approachable.
- Accessibility: excellent for casual viewers; little friction, big charm.
Tradeoff:
It is less surprising than the top three if you want something especially original or discussion-provoking. But if your date-night goal is comfort, chemistry, and style, it delivers.
5) The Princess Bride
- Great if you want something sweet, funny, and light.
- Tone: fairy-tale romance with comedy and adventure.
- Pacing: easygoing and breezy.
- Accessibility: broadly accessible, especially if both of you enjoy witty older favorites.
Tradeoff:
Its knowingly storybook tone can feel a little arch or old-fashioned for viewers wanting modern romantic chemistry. It’s more charming than emotionally intense.
Why the Others Didn’t Make the Top 5
Option 1:   Ocean’s Eleven     Sleek, funny, ultra-watchable heist movie   Great pacing, lower romance factor
View details
Option 2:   Before Sunrise     Intimate, talky, deeply romantic   Best for the right mood, less casual-viewer friendly
View details
Option 3:   Arrival     Thoughtful, moving sci-fi with emotional weight   Strong film, weaker fit for “avoid depressing endings”
View details
Quick elimination notes
-   Ocean’s Eleven  : very date-friendly and stylish, but less emotionally romantic than your final five. If you want “cool” over “romantic,” it could replace   The Princess Bride  .
-   Before Sunrise  : arguably the most romantic film on the list, but it depends heavily on patience for conversation-driven cinema. Amazing for the right pair, riskier for casual viewers.
-   Arrival  : excellent movie, but more meditative and bittersweet. For your “avoid overly depressing endings” constraint, it’s a softer fit.
Best Pick by Date-Night Mood
-   Most universally safe choice:     Palm Springs
-   Best if you want lively banter and plot:     Knives Out
-   Best animated choice:     Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
-   Best classic comfort watch:     The Princess Bride
-   Best glossy modern romance:     Crazy Rich Asians
